findings.diagnosis: The prompt is too reluctant to split off sentence-introductory function words (initial determiners, prepositional/adverbial leads); these safe, very short left pieces often improve streaming fidelity in low-latency bins.
findings.evidence: en_us_292, en_us_845, en_us_884, en_us_482, en_us_46 — each target inserted an early cut (at or immediately after the sentence intro/determiner/adverbial) and gained H_set in short-latency bins; they share that the right-hand material did not require unresolved antecedents or scope.

edit.text: Allow splits immediately after sentence-introductory function words (initial determiners, prepositional or adverbial leads) when the remaining right-hand piece is semantically self-contained and does not rely on unresolved antecedents or scope to be true.

findings.diagnosis: A blanket prohibition on cutting immediately after main verbs is applied too widely; many short, self-contained predicates or closed prepositional complements are safe to emit separately and help dense, low-latency segmentation.
findings.evidence: en_us_164, en_us_340, en_us_924 — in each case the target allowed a cut that isolates a short predicate or closed complement (e.g. short clause or prepositional phrase) and improved cohesion without creating contradiction.

edit.text: Do not ban cuts after a main verb universally; permit a cut when the right-hand piece forms a short, independent predicate or closed complement (no unresolved scope, antecedent, or polarity dependence).

findings.diagnosis: The prompt fails to protect tight numeral+unit and quantifier+noun spans; splitting numerals from their units or quantified noun leads to severe cohesion loss.
findings.evidence: en_us_278, en_us_860, en_us_1024 — each target kept numerals/quantifiers attached to their units or quantified noun ('46 percent', 'over 10 years', 'two summer Olympics') and gained H_set versus policies that separated them.

edit.text: Do not cut between a numeral/quantifier and its unit or quantified noun; treat numeral+unit (or quantifier+noun) as an atomic span for segmentation.
